title: Ulyana and the Language
premise: Emrys Crane, once the conservatory's most celebrated composition student, returns two decades later as its night janitor, hiding behind a mop and a name no one remembers. When a late-night radio broadcast airs a melody Emrys wrote at nineteen and never recorded—a piece believed lost with their mentor, Ulyana Voss—Emrys realizes someone has kept it alive, and that the conservatory's scheduled demolition will bury whatever truth remains. Following the song's provenance through old letters, a estranged former lover now on the demolition board, and Ulyana's deaf granddaughter who 'hears' music through vibration, Emrys uncovers the sentence Ulyana left untranslated in her final manuscript: a confession about whose hand truly wrote the work that made them both famous. In the end, Emrys translates the sentence publicly on the eve of demolition—admitting the masterpiece was Ulyana's, stolen by ambition—and chooses to stay visible, teaching the granddaughter the language of the music as the walls come down.
about_author: Orsen Amberdale is the pen name of a former conservatory custodian who spent eleven years sweeping concert halls before publishing a debut story collection praised for its 'tender attention to forgotten rooms.' They live near a decommissioned music school and write at night, when the radiators sing.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Emrys Crane's POV. Establishes Emrys's nightly routine mopping the conservatory's practice halls, moving invisibly among students who never look up. A flashback flicker: the last time they stood here as a prodigy. Emotional beat: the ache of chosen smallness, and the first crack in it when Emrys pauses too long outside Room 7, their old studio.

chapters.title: A Song That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Alone in the boiler room, the radio plays a piece Emrys wrote at nineteen and destroyed—'Vesper, Unfinished,' never recorded, never performed. The announcer credits it to Ulyana Voss's estate. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past reaching through the static to claim them. Emrys drops a bottle of cleaner and lets it spill.

chapters.title: Demolition Date
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Notices posted: the conservatory closes in ninety days. Emrys learns the board chair is Halvard Reyes—the lover they abandoned twenty years ago. Emotional beat: dread braided with longing; the building and the heart share the same countdown. Emrys signs the acknowledgment form with a shaking hand.

chapters.title: Ulyana's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Introduces Sefa Voss, POV alternating briefly to her. Deaf since childhood, Sefa visits the empty halls to press her palms against the piano soundboards, feeling music as weather. She is cataloging her grandmother's papers before the wreckers come. Emotional beat: quiet defiance—she refuses to let the archive be landfill.

chapters.title: Room 7
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Cleaning Room 7 after hours, Emrys finds a loose floorboard and beneath it a tin box: Ulyana's final manuscript, its last page bearing one untranslated sentence in her private notation. Emotional beat: terror and gravity; holding the box feels like holding a lit fuse. Emrys pockets it instead of turning it in.

chapters.title: Halvard
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. First confrontation with Halvard Reyes at a board meeting Emrys attends in janitor's coveralls. Halvard recognizes them instantly and says nothing—weaponized silence. Emotional beat: shame curdling into resolve; Emrys realizes invisibility is a debt now being called in.

chapters.title: The Notation
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa discovers Emrys studying her grandmother's cipher in the archive and confronts the janitor who shouldn't know what a plagal cadence is. Recognition scene: she realizes who Emrys is. Emotional beat: suspicion giving way to a wary alliance—two people guarding the same fire from opposite sides.

chapters.title: What the Radio Knew
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys traces the broadcast to a small station and its host, an aging archivist who received tapes anonymously for years. Someone has been leaking Ulyana's unreleased works—one per month, like a countdown. Emotional beat: paranoia and wonder; a ghost with a purpose. Emrys begins to suspect the sender wants the truth forced into daylight.

chapters.title: Lessons in Vibration
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa asks Emrys to teach her 'Vesper, Unfinished' so she can feel it properly. Their lessons in the emptied rehearsal room become the book's warm center. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness; Emrys hears their own young voice in every phrase and starts to grieve what they threw away.

chapters.title: Letters, Burned at the Edges
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Among Ulyana's papers, letters reveal the famous 'Crane Variations' were based on her sketches—and that she knew, and said nothing, for love or leverage. Emotional beat: the floor tilting; Emrys's entire identity as 'the prodigy' was built on borrowed ground.

chapters.title: The Board Votes
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV (first time). Halvard pushes the demolition through early, partly to bury the scandal the leaked recordings are stirring, partly to wound the past. Emotional beat: bitter clarity—Halvard loved Emrys enough to hate the building that took them. The date moves up: forty days.

chapters.title: Interlude: The Radiator Song
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A short chapter of stillness: Sefa records the building itself—pipes, wind in the organ loft, the elevator hum—and layers them into something like music. Emotional beat: elegy; the conservatory is already becoming an instrument played by its own leaving. She gives the recording to Emrys without explanation.

chapters.title: Confession, Drafted
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys attempts to decode Ulyana's final sentence using the notation key hidden in the margins of old exercise books. Partial translation yields fragments: 'the hands were mine / the name was yours / I chose this.' Emotional beat: vertigo inverted—perhaps Ulyana gave away credit deliberately, and Emrys's theft was invited.

chapters.title: Halvard's Archive
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard has been quietly buying Ulyana's papers for years—and is revealed as the anonymous radio sender, drip-feeding the truth toward the demolition date. Emotional beat: revelation reframes the antagonist; Halvard's sabotage is a love letter written in evidence.

chapters.title: The Leak Becomes a Flood
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs via news clippings and student chatter. The leaked recordings go viral; journalists swarm the condemned building; the 'Crane Variations' authorship becomes public controversy while Emrys mops around reporters. Emotional beat: claustrophobia—visibility arriving all at once, like floodwater.

chapters.title: What Sefa Heard
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa finishes learning 'Vesper' and, feeling its structure through the floor, notices a passage that only makes sense as a musical signature—Ulyana's handwriting embedded in the score Emrys always claimed. She confronts Emrys gently. Emotional beat: heartbreak without cruelty; the student out-hears the teacher.

chapters.title: Nineteen Again
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A long flashback chapter: the night twenty years ago when Emrys, panicked and ambitious, submitted Ulyana's sketchbook work under their own name—and the morning Ulyana looked at them and smiled anyway. Emotional beat: the full weight of the original sin, rendered without excuse.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, alone at night. With Sefa's insight and the margin key, Emrys completes the translation: 'I gave you my name so you would have somewhere to stand; stand somewhere true before the walls forget us both.' Emotional beat: devastation transfigured into instruction—Ulyana's last gift was not absolution but a deadline.

chapters.title: Eve of the Wrecking Ball
chapters.summary: Climax. At the final board meeting, with Halvard presiding and cameras outside, Emrys stands in coveralls and reads the translated sentence aloud, publicly renouncing authorship of the Variations. Emotional beat: the terrifying freedom of truth; Halvard's face breaking open; the room's long silence before anyone breathes.

chapters.title: Demolition Day
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, anchored by Sefa. As machines arrive, Sefa performs 'Vesper, Unfinished' on the steps—feeling it through the ground while the crowd falls silent—and Emrys stands beside her, named and unhidden. Emotional beat: grief and release braided; the building ends as it began, full of music.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Open Score
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Weeks later: the authorship correction is published, Halvard and Emrys meet without armor and part without promise, and the archive finds a home in a university library. Emotional beat: quiet repair; nothing restored, everything acknowledged. Emrys keeps the tin box, now empty, on a windowsill.

chapters.title: First Lesson
chapters.summary: Final chapter, shared Emrys/Sefa POV. In a rented room with a secondhand piano, Emrys begins formally teaching Sefa composition—her way, through touch and vibration—writing a new method they call, simply, the Language. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled; the last line mirrors the first, but now Emrys owns the room they stand in.
